papers.title: Quot schemes on projective space
papers.abstract: We develop general methods for studying Quot schemes on projective space, including a new construction of components with no common neighbours. We show that the radius of Hilbert and Quot schemes can grow linearly with the dimension of the subschemes being parametrized, and construct the first examples of Hilbert schemes of curves with radius two. For absolutely split bundles on projective space, we construct a distinguished generically smooth component and classify all smooth Quot schemes. In most cases, we give explicit geometric descriptions in terms of products of generalized flag varieties and projective bundles over Grassmannians.

papers.title: Genus one mirror symmetry and surfaces with trivial first Chern class
papers.abstract: The main goal of this paper is to study the extension of genus-one BCOV type mirror symmetry for smooth projective varieties with vanishing $c_1(X)$. We show that the naive generalization of the expectation that one can encode genus one Gromov-Witten invariants in the BCOV invariant of the mirror family cannot hold in this setup. We show this by completing the study of these invariants for surfaces. Progress had been made recently by Oberdieck's proof of the Klemm-Mariño conjecture for Enriques surfaces, which can be combined with computations of equivariant analytic torsion by Yoshikawa. We also perform the analogous study for bielliptic surfaces. Both of these cases present a sign issue not present in the known trivial canonical bundle cases, which we show implies that the mirror symmetry predictions cannot hold for varieties with torsion canonical bundle, even up to sign.

papers.title: The Dolbeault geometric Langlands-type conjecture for smooth surfaces
papers.abstract: Using a general theory of limit categories for symmetric stacks, we construct their semiorthogonal decompositions for moduli stacks of pure one-dimensional coherent sheaves on smooth surfaces with nef anti-canonical divisors. The components of these semiorthogonal decompositions are quasi-BPS categories associated with the corresponding local Calabi--Yau threefolds. By comparing these semiorthogonal decompositions with those of dg-categories of coherent sheaves on moduli stacks of semistable sheaves, we propose a Dolbeault geometric Langlands-type conjecture for surfaces, generalizing the Dolbeault geometric Langlands conjecture for $\GL_r$-Higgs bundles. Our conjecture includes a correspondence for Higgs bundles twisted by sufficiently ample line bundles on curves. We discuss examples and construct Hecke actions on limit categories and, under certain conditions, on quasi-BPS categories. For symplectic surfaces, these actions are expected to provide a categorical lift of the corresponding Hecke operators on BPS cohomology constructed by Davison--Hennecart--Kinjo--Schiffmann--Vasserot.

papers.title: Semiorthogonal decompositions of limit categories for symmetric stacks
papers.abstract: In our earlier work with Tudor Padurariu, we introduced the notion of limit categories for derived stacks with self-dual cotangent complexes and used them to formulate the Dolbeault geometric Langlands conjecture. In this paper, we generalize the notion of limit categories to a broader class of derived stacks, which we call symmetric stacks. One of the motivations for this generalization is to formulate Dolbeault geometric Langlands-type correspondences for a broader class of moduli stacks. We establish several fundamental properties of limit categories for symmetric stacks, including compact generation, the existence of semiorthogonal decompositions, functoriality, and a Kunneth formula. In a companion paper, we apply the results of this paper to formulate a Dolbeault geometric Langlands-type conjecture for moduli stacks of sheaves on smooth surfaces with nef anticanonical divisors.

papers.title: Gerbe-corrected stringy E-functions
papers.abstract: We define an invariant of $\mathbb{Q}$-Gorenstein complex varieties with at worst log-terminal singularities equipped with a rational Brauer class $α$ that generalizes existing versions of the $α$-corrected stringy $E$-polynomial, which are defined only for quotients of quasi-projective varieties by finite groups. Using recent results from $p$-adic integration, this new invariant can be shown to behave well for degenerate dual abelian fibrations and to agree with the intersection or BPS $E$-polynomial for certain moduli problems.

papers.title: Tensor powers of the Steinberg character of $GL_n(\mathbb{F}_q)$, zonotopal algebras, and quiver varieties
papers.abstract: In this paper we study the $m$-th tensor power ${\rm St}^{\otimes m}$ of the Steinberg character of $GL_n(q)$. To do that we use the connection between tensor products of unipotent characters and the cohomology of certain quiver varieties for star-shaped quivers \cite{L2}\cite{LRV}. We prove that the cohomology ring of the quiver variety associated to ${\rm St}^{\otimes m}$ is generated by its tautological classes. We use this to prove that this cohomology ring is isomorphic to a central zonotopal algebra. We then deduce a combinatorial formula for the multiplicities of unipotent characters in ${\rm St}^{\otimes m}$. This formula has been conjectured by the second author when $m=2$.

papers.title: GIT-thresholds for K-moduli spaces of Hypersurfaces
papers.abstract: In this note, we confirm the first wall $c_1(d)$ of K-moduli of hypersurfaces of degree $d$ in $\mathbb P^n$ for $n\geq 3$ and $d\geq n+1$, where $c_1(d)=\frac{n+1}{nd}$ if $d$ is even; and $c_1(d)=\frac{n+1}{nd-(n+1)}$ if $d$ is odd. Before this wall, the K-moduli is identical to the GIT-moduli for degree $d$ hypersurfaces, so we also call this number the GIT-threshold.

papers.title: The generalized Franchetta conjecture for some hyper-Kähler varieties, III
papers.abstract: The generalized Franchetta conjecture states that for a locally complete family of polarized hyper-Kähler varieties, the generically defined cycles on any fiber of the universal family over the moduli stack inject into cohomology via the cycle class map. We prove the generalized Franchetta conjecture for the family of double EPW sextics discovered by O'Grady and for the family of double EPW cubes discovered by Iliev-Kapustka-Kapustka-Ranestad. We also prove a Franchetta-type result for the relative square of the universal family of double EPW sextics, which allows to relate double EPW sextics and Gushel-Mukai fourfolds on the level of motives. The proof involves the geometry of Gushel-Mukai fourfolds, whose Kuznetsov component allows to realize double EPW sextics and cubes as moduli spaces of Bridgeland-stable objects, relatively over the parameter space of Gushel-Mukai fourfolds. A key step is that the canonical Chow-Künneth decomposition of special Gushel-Mukai fourfolds is multiplicative; we use this to show that generically defined cycles on the third power of a special Gushel-Mukai fourfold inject into cohomology via the cycle class map. Along the way, we also show that the canonical Chow-Künneth decomposition of any Gushel-Mukai sixfold is multiplicative.
